newsitem.title: UK: Rushdie supporters condemn EU decision on Iran.
newsitem.headline: Rushdie supporters condemn EU decision on Iran.

text.p: Supporters of Salman Rushdie on Tuesday condemned the European Union's decision to allow its ambassadors to return to Tehran while an Iranian death threat is still hanging over the British author.

The ambassadors were withdrawn after a German court accused Iran's rulers of ordering political assassinations in Europe. But the EU decided on Tuesday to allow them to return, although it suspended ministerial meetings with Iran.

"The EU Council of Ministers' decision is shocking, particularly when we know that they are fully aware of Iran's involvement in many other acts of terrorism in Europe," said Carmel Bedford, secretary of the London-based International Rushdie Defence Committee.
"Their action is not so much a slap on the wrist, it's more a nod and a wink to Iran. It sends a clear message that Iran can get away with murder in Europe," she said in a statement.

The death edict or fatwa on Rushdie was issued in 1989 by Iran's then spiritual leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini because of alleged blasphemy against Islam in Rushdie's novel "The Satanic Verses". Rushdie has been in hiding ever since.
The connittee said only "selective sanctions" would be effective in exerting pressure on Iran to lift the fatwa.

"We urge the EU to rethink its policy on Iran and act decisively to deter future acts of terrorism and to convince EU citizens that economic trade and commerce with Iran will not be allowed to compromise their freedom of expression and other fundamental human rights," Bedford said.
Earlier, Britain said it fully supported the EU decision to suspend ministerial ties with Iran.
"The message to Iran is clear -- there can be no 'business as usual'," the Foreign Office said in a statement.
"Together with our EU partners we will be watching Iran's behaviour more closely than ever. Future development of relations depend on her," it said.
